behavior.definition: Behavior Change Index (0-100) = mean of four 0-1 scaled items: approved-tool use days/5, tasks augmented (capped at 8)/8, (self-rated prompt sophistication-1)/4, human-in-the-loop practices/4. Paired change = same person's index at d30/d60/d90 minus their baseline (entry tier only).

self_vs_observed.note: People with both a facilitator observation and a d60/d90 self-rating. Positive gap = self-rating above observed.

did.caveat: NOT a causal estimate. People chose when to enrol, so early and later groups differ in interest and in how fast their AI use was already growing. A non-zero placebo (pre-period) gap means parallel trends fails; the trend-adjusted figure assumes the pre-period gap continues linearly, which is itself an assumption. Only a randomized or lottery-based rollout of seats would support a causal claim. Pulse respondents are a self-selected ~1/3 sample.
did.design: Staggered adoption with not-yet-trained comparison. Early = completed the entry tier (AI Explorer / AI Ready Leaders) in Oct-Dec 2025 (waves W1-W2). Later = completed it in Apr-Jun 2026 (W4-W5), so they were not yet trained at the Jan 2026 pulse.
did.outcome: Campus AI pulse: approved-tool use, workdays per week (0-5)

synthetic_validation.label: SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY: the true effect is known because we generated it. Real data has no such answer key.
synthetic_validation.note: Average built-in training effect on true weekly tool-use days for entry-tier completers trained by Dec 2025, evaluated at the Jan 2026 campus pulse (before measurement noise and 0-5 clipping). Known only because the data are synthetic.

enabling.note: Manager-support band from the person's baseline follow-up. Differences are associations, not effects of manager support.

meta.title: AI Adoption Impact Scorecard

not_shown: Any individual's participation, scores, survey answers or tool use. Every figure is a group of at least 10 people; smaller groups show "<10".
Causal impact. The early-vs-later comparison is a difference-in-differences on self-selected groups with one short pre-period; it is descriptive, not proof that training caused the change.
Work quality or accuracy of AI-assisted output. Hours returned are self-estimates for adopted use cases, partly validated, and are capacity, not budget savings.
People who never answered a follow-up. Engaged people answer more often and response falls by day 90 (see cohort retention), so follow-up results are likely optimistic.
Use of non-approved AI tools, or approved-tool use outside the three admin reports. Telemetry counts accounts active in a month, not tasks or time saved.
Whether a unit or role family is 'behind'. Units differ in role mix, computer access and work content; heat-map colors compare a unit to other units, not to a target.
Job or headcount effects. Nothing here estimates AI replacement of roles; it measures learning and applied use.
Sensitive-data compliance. Use-case data classification and human-in-the-loop checklists are self-reported at intake.
Who should be hired, promoted or named a successor. The talent view is aggregate and associational; badge holders already moved more before they earned the badge.

inter_rater.description: Frames the task, context, constraints and audience in the prompt
Checks output for accuracy, bias and fit; cites what was verified
Applies data classification, approved-tool and disclosure rules
Integrates the tool into a repeatable work process with a human decision point

proficiency.note: Human-scored rubric (1-4) on the applied-component artifact (AI Catalyst role scenario, cohort capstones); ~25% double-scored by two raters. Proficient = artifact mean >= 2.5 with no criterion below 2. Rater identities are never published.

unit_training.note: Unit Training sessions are requested by a unit for its own staff. They count toward reach, not toward a badge tier.

talent.goal: Series goal (public goals page): badges should guide internal talent marketplace opportunities and inform workforce planning and succession strategies, and should develop 'super AI users'.
guardrails: Aggregate only. No list of badge holders goes to hiring managers or succession committees from this scorecard.

Badges are voluntary and access is uneven by role family (see access ratio). Using a badge as a screening or ranking criterion could create disparate impact; treat it as an opt-in signal the employee chooses to share in the talent marketplace.

If any automated tool uses badges to rank or screen candidates, Illinois HB 3773 notice and anti-discrimination duties apply; civil-service and bargaining-unit rules may also limit use. Legal and labor-relations review first.
Higher talent-event rates after a badge are associations. The same people already had higher rates before the badge (self-selection); compare 'before' with 'after' before reading anything into it.

succession.note: Share of distinct people named on successor slates who held an applied badge when named, vs the share of the eligible pool (leaders, academic professionals, faculty) holding one.

talent.super_ai_user_definition: Holder of the top badge on either track (AI Practitioner or AI Forward Strategies).

telemetry.note: Unit-month aggregates from admin reports. Active and repeat users cannot be de-duplicated across tools, so tools are shown separately. Licensed population differs by tool (ChatGPT Edu is seat-based).
